Hi Ava —

Attached our redline and a short list of our non-negotiables so you can flag them to legal:

- Residency: Pilot must be EU-only (data-at-rest physically in EU). Production may be US/EU but pilot is EU-only.
- Subprocessors: we require 30-day notice + right to object to new subprocessors; please supply current list and a cadence for updates.
- Breach notify: initial notice within 48 hours of detection to our security@greenfieldlabs.io, with hourly cadence for critical incidents until contained; please confirm if Redwood can meet 48 hours.
- Logs: we need access to per-request audit logs for the pilot, retained for 90 days. We also want examples of the logging format (fields) and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM.
- PII classification: we classified three categories as highly sensitive (patient data, financial identifiers, auth tokens) — confirm processing restrictions.

I've attached: Greenfield_DPA_redline_20270603.pdf (redline) and a short comments summary.

Thanks,
Sofia Rinaldi
Head of Product Security, Greenfield Labs

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Greenfield redline — initial legal notes

Ava / team — forwarding my initial read on Sofia's redline and the asks. High-level comments and recommended next messages: 

1) Residency: We can offer EU-only residency for the pilot using EU-only clusters and restricting routing. We need to document the hosting region and the SCADA/infra controls. I'll coordinate with infra to produce a short statement and a diagram.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a current subprocessors list and publishes changes via our portal. 30-day notice and objection right is higher than standard; propose: 30-day notice + right to object for 'legitimate reasons' and an escalation path with privacy team. Legal happy to offer a compromise text — see suggested wording below.

Suggested compromise wording (to send to Greenfield):
"Redwood will provide written notice of any new subprocessor at least 30 days in advance. Customer may raise a reasonable objection within that period; parties will engage in good faith to resolve. If unresolved, Customer may request continued use be conditioned on execution of standard subcontractor safeguards or use of alternative subprocessors, subject to feasibility."

3) Breach notify: 48 hours initial notification is aggressive but feasible for confirmed incidents where scope is known. For suspected incidents we normally commit to 'as soon as practicable' and to provide initial acknowledgement within 72 hours while we triage. Recommend proposing: initial acknowledgement within 48 hours for confirmed incidents, 72-hour acknowledgement window for suspected incidents, with hourly updates for critical incidents during active containment.

4) Logs/exports: We can provide per-request audit logs for the pilot via a secure S3 export or direct SIEM push; retention configurable up to 90 days. Need SRE to confirm retention limits and export format. I'll request sample export schema and a redacted SOC2 snapshot (we can provide redacted PDF).

5) PII categories: We'll map the three categories Sofia listed to our data classification and provide handling constraints (no training on customer-provided PII for pilot unless explicitly allowed, masking suggestions).

Next steps I recommend:
- Ava: send Sofia a one-pager that confirms the pilot can be EU-only and outlines the proposed breach-notify compromise and subprocessor language.
- Rishi/Legal: I'll prepare the suggested DPA language and request SOC2 redacted PDF from compliance.
- Monica/Engineering: please attach sample audit log schema and confirm whether we can push exports to their SIEM (Splunk).

I'll draft legal text by EOD tomorrow.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Hi Sofia / Markus —

Thanks for the redline and clear list — appreciate the level of detail. Quick consolidated response and the materials we promised: 

1) Residency: We can run the pilot on EU-only infrastructure. I'll attach a short infrastructure statement and a deployment diagram to confirm physical hosting.

2) Subprocessors: We publish a subprocessors list and can provide 30-day notice. Legal (Rishi) has suggested compromise wording — included below for your review. If that looks ok, we can include it in a DPA addendum.

3) Breach notification: Per Rishi's note, we propose:
   - Confirmed incidents: initial notice within 48 hours of confirmation.
   - Suspected incidents: acknowledgment within 72 hours while triage continues.
   - For critical incidents we will provide hourly updates until containment.

4) Logs & retention: We can provide per-request audit logs and export them to your SIEM (Splunk) via secure S3 transfer or direct push. Retention can be set to 90 days for the pilot; sample schema attached.

5) PII handling: We will map the three sensitive categories and propose masking/processing constraints; no training on customer provided PII during the pilot unless explicitly requested and contracted.

Attached: SOC2_snapshot_redacted.pdf (redacted), infra_deployment_statement.pdf (short), audit_log_schema_example.csv

Next steps:
- Can we set a legal-to-legal call Thursday 10am CET / 1am PT (I know that's early; if not, propose 9am CET) to iron the DPA language? Rishi will bring suggested text.
- I'll upload the materials to the shared Drive and add the HubSpot record (HS-98321) with links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Redwood-Compliance-SOC2

If you want we can also produce a one-page data-responsibility matrix by EOD Thursday.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.
